descriptions: stainless, motionless, eternal, actionless, attributeless, great, sky-like knowledge and bliss (GŚ 99)
the samarasa of body and supreme state (SSP 5)
the state where the mind sees the mind in sahaja-samādhi (AmŚ 54)
negations: fearless, supportless, without elaboration, without resting-place, formless (GŚ 92)
relation_to_self: The self is Śiva; the yogī enters the supreme 'like milk into milk' and becomes non-dual (GŚ 100); the guru's grace unites body and pada.
relation_to_world: The whole cosmos is within the body (piṇḍa-brahmāṇḍa); the body is to be perfected, not merely transcended.
caveat: The Nāth texts affirm one supreme under many names and place all schools beneath it, but they insist that it is reached through the body and the guru, not through scripture or reasoning; a one-truth reading that ignores the body-centred path would misstate them.

descriptions: all-pervading, ever-risen, undivided, independent, spotless; by its will creation and in it dissolution (KJN 3.9–10)
all is samarasa, full, the Akulavīra alone (Akulavīra A.41)
negations: not in the supports, aims, channels or breaths; neither near nor far; beyond is and is not (Akulavīra A.15–23, A.34)
relation_to_self: The jīva is the supreme Śiva, called jīva while in the body (KJN 6.4–7); the self is its own guru (17.35).
relation_to_world: Creation and dissolution occur within the body; the Kula (Śakti's domain) and Akula (Śiva) are inseparable.
caveat: The Yoginīkaula's one reality is reached through Kaula practice and secrecy; it declares all other schools bound in conceptual construction (Akulavīra A.7–10), so it would not accept being placed as one view among equals.

descriptions: Śiva present equally in what is pure and impure, feared and loved
the state beyond the eight fetters, in which the bound paśu becomes Maheśvara (Kulārṇava 13.91)
relation_to_self: The one freed from the fetters is himself Maheśvara; the guru is Śiva.
relation_to_world: The world, including the cremation ground and what is loathed, is not other than Śiva.
caveat: Aghora's own texts (Kīnārām's Vivekasār etc.) are not yet extracted; this view rests on the shared Kaula doctrine of the fetters and on the lineage's self-description, and should be revised from its own writings.

descriptions: the divine as the Mother of all, served in the sick and the outcaste
relation_to_self: The same Aghora teaching of non-difference, turned toward service.
relation_to_world: The world is served, not shunned.
caveat: Recent movement; formulation from general reports, not from its own texts.
